subject: On‑prem commercial unbundling & SLA crediting — proposal and questions
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@hearth.ai>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.inference>
Cc: procurement@hearth.ai
Date: Tue, 05 May 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Hearth Labs — commercial questions on private deployment pricing

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for the demo last week — felt very promising. Procurement asked me to get clarity on how Redwood is pricing private deployments for our multi‑site rollout. Two items specifically:

1) Can you break out the platform fee vs licensed node/node‑seat fee? We need to show CAPEX vs OPEX split to our finance team.
2) What credits or support concessions do you offer for a 3‑site pilot (12 months) that escalates to ~150 nodes in year two? Any starter credits, implementation retainer offsets, or SLA crediting mechanics we should plan for?

I attached the SOW draft (see heartbeat section) with rough timeline — can you review and advise on an example commercial construct we could present to execs?

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Head of IT Programs
Hearth Labs

Attachments: Hearth_SOW_v3.pdf (PDF, 245KB)
From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.inference>
To: Elena Morales <elena@hearth.ai>
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.inference>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 05 May 2026 11:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hearth Labs — commercial questions on private deployment pricing

Elena — thanks, and really appreciate the SOW. Quick summary below; Laura and Aditya are copied to weigh in on legal/pricing specifics:

- Platform fee: fixed annual fee that covers control plane, observability, and ongoing SLAs. Typically amortized as OPEX but can be capitalized depending on your procurement rules.
- Licensed nodes: per‑node license with optional meter for GPU consumption. These are often treated as CAPEX in customer accounting and can be invoiced as upfront or spread monthly.
- Starter credits: for pilot customers we can provide a one‑time implementation credit (reduces platform fee for first 3 months) plus engineering hours for onboarding as a time‑boxed retainer.
- SLA crediting: standard SLA credits apply for downtime. For private placements we also offer a limited service‑credit escrow that increases with committed nodes (we can discuss thresholds).

Would you be open to a sample breakout with three constructs: pilot (3 sites, 12 months), growth (roll to 3 regions, 50 nodes), and scale (150 nodes year two)? I can draft ranges and a model.

—Vivek
VP, Commercial
Redwood Inference
From: Elena Morales <elena@hearth.ai>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.inference>
Cc: procurement@hearth.ai
Date: Wed, 06 May 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hearth Labs — commercial questions on private deployment pricing

Vivek — yes, a three‑construct model would be ideal. A couple of additional asks from procurement and finance:

- Can the platform fee be tiered by active tokens or aggregated across all sites? They want clarity on unit economics.
- For the pilot, procurement prefers credits applied as invoice line‑item discounts (not one‑off SOW credits) — easier for our bookkeeping.
- Is there a mobility clause for nodes (e.g., reassign license seats between sites during pilot) without penalty?

Also attached a quick checklist procurement completed — would appreciate any redlines on the term sheet.

Best,
Elena

Attachments: Procurement_Checklist.xlsx (XLSX, 32KB)
From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.inference>
To: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.inference>, aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 07 May 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Hearth Labs — commercial questions on private deployment pricing

Laura / Aditya — forwarding Hearth's asks. Key commercial decisions we need to align on before I send a formal proposal:

1) Platform fee treatment: offer two billing constructs — annual platform fee (standard) or amortized monthly with a 6% premium. For the pilot I suggest amortized monthly to lower up‑front cash.
2) Starter credits: propose a $75k implementation credit for the pilot applied as an invoice credit across the first 3 months. Procurement wants invoice‑line discounts; legal to confirm wording for invoice crediting.
3) Mobility: allow seat reassignments up to 20% of pilot seats without penalty; anything beyond requires 30‑day notice.
4) SLA credits / escrow: offer a capped 3% service credit pool that grows to 6% on passage to >50 nodes. This is a strong signal without unbounded exposure.

Aditya — can you run pricing math on these two constructs (annual vs amortized) and produce a simple table (pilot / growth / scale) with list price, proposed discount, and net ARR / committed spend? Laura — can you draft the invoice credit language and call out any risk areas (tax/accounting treatment implications)?

Thanks — I want to get Hearth a clean commercial by next Tuesday.

—Vivek
From: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.inference>
To: Elena Morales <elena@hearth.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.inference>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 15:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed commercial constructs & next steps — Hearth Labs (HEA-2026-042)

Elena — thanks for the patience. Attached is our proposed commercial summary and term sheet snapshot. High level:

Pilot construct (3 sites, 12 months):
- Platform fee (amortized monthly): $45,000/month
- Licensed nodes: $1,200/node/month (up to 30 nodes), mobility allowance: up to 6 nodes can be reassigned between sites without penalty during pilot
- Implementation credit: $75,000 applied as invoice credit across months 1–3 (line item: Pilot Implementation Credit)
- SLA crediting: 3% capped service credit pool during pilot

Growth construct (rolling to region +50 nodes):
- Platform fee: $540,000/year (annual election) with 10% volume discount once >50 nodes
- Node price steps down to $950/node/month at >50 nodes
- Escalation credit: one‑time migration credit equal to 1 month of platform fee when committing to multi‑region deployment

Scale construct (150 nodes):
- Committed discount schedule and extended SRE retainer options. Proposed commercial doc links and DocuSign prepared here: https://docusign.example.com/HEA-2026-042

Next steps:
1) Laura to confirm invoice‑credit language (cc'd).
2) Elena / procurement to confirm preferred billing cadence (monthly amortized vs annual).
3) If accepted, we'll prepare final term sheet + DocuSign and align on implementation milestones.

Happy to hop on a 30min call to walk through the numbers — propose Wed 14th at 9a PT.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_Term_Sheet.xlsx (XLSX, 120KB), Commercial_Summary_HEA-2026-042.pdf (PDF, 68KB)
